title: What angles do the creases of a paper craft make?
description: A paper craft is made by following the pictured folds, then opened out fully. Lines are drawn along the creases and the angles they form are measured with a protractor, and a fold that lays one arm over another is checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: a crease is a straight line, and a fold that lays one arm over another bisects the angle. Watch for students who measure from the wrong arm on the opened paper.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q8
video_script.why: The child opens out a folded craft, draws lines along the creases and measures the angles by the three checks of the solved example.
video_script.substitution: The creases of the paper craft of the book's pictured folds.
video_script.anchor: the pictured folds of the book's paper craft, and the creases on the opened paper
video_script.payoff_line: A fold that lays one arm over another makes two equal angles

final_answer.value: open-ended; a fold that lays one arm over another makes two equal angles

maths_rules: the question is open-ended, so the readings depend on the folds made
a fold makes a crease, and a crease is a straight line
a fold that lays one arm over another is the angle bisector, so the two angles it makes read the same
video_script.design: A folded sheet is opened on the board. Lines are drawn along the creases, the angles are measured, and the equal pair made by a bisecting fold is held back until the answer line.
open_questions: The book gives the craft only as eight pictured folds, with no names or numbers, so the video stays general and never names the craft.
